flashcard_questions.q: Why was Dickens's father imprisoned when Dickens was twelve?
What product did the factory where young Dickens worked make?
flashcard_questions.a: Boot blacking, a kind of shoe polish.

flashcard_questions.q: Which term means a narrative longer than a short story but shorter than a novel?
What form had Dickens first planned before he chose to write a story?
Which city was Dickens walking in when he decided on a story instead?
Which institution was the only safety net for destitute Victorians?
Why were conditions inside the workhouse made deliberately harsh?
flashcard_questions.a: To discourage people from seeking help.

flashcard_questions.q: What did the Victorian upper classes believe caused poverty?
flashcard_questions.a: Laziness or moral failure, rather than an unjust system.

flashcard_questions.q: What did Malthus argue about unchecked population growth?
flashcard_questions.a: That it would outstrip food supply and resources.

flashcard_questions.q: Which phrase of Scrooge's echoes Malthusian thinking?

flashcard_questions.a: 60% of men and 40% of women could read.

flashcard_questions.q: Why did Dickens set his story at Christmas?
flashcard_questions.a: People were already in a mood of generosity and goodwill.

flashcard_questions.q: Which genre supplies the ghost, the fog and the supernatural visitations?
What is a stave in music?
flashcard_questions.a: The set of five horizontal lines on which notes are written.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Shakespeare play does Dickens allude to at the opening of Stave 1?

notes: 15 cards: 8 context-to-relevance (Dickens's father, the blacking factory, the pamphlet, Manchester, the workhouse, upper-class attitudes, Malthus, literacy), 3 cause cards (harsh workhouses, the Christmas setting, the reason for poverty), 2 definition-front term cards (novella, stave), 1 genre card, 1 quotation card. Dropped the literary-allusion and blacking-factory glossary entries as definition cards — both are tested through the Hamlet and factory context cards, so a second direction would interfere.
